evidence_state: Decoded static contracts; no live-system claims
selection_reason: This is the next coherent high-effect family: one command stages deferred peripheral-controller resets, two expose reset/status state, and one synchronizes status into cfgdb.
sharing_model: All four addresses are distinct functions in the exact same libscbmccore binary. The state-machine relationship is shared; wire layouts, flags, side effects, and completion behavior remain per-address overlays. No implementation identity with another BMC is claimed.

common_overlay.internal_authorization: No additional caller identity or role check decoded inside these four handlers
common_overlay.platform: All four require numeric platform type 2
common_overlay.safety: State-changing routes remain non-runnable; deferred callback and physical-device consequences are not decoded here

operations.request_contract: The wrapper passes the outer request length separately but the decoded helper does not consume it. Data byte0 is copied into pending-reset state. Data byte1 is a target/mask selector and must be 1, 2, or 3. The handler has no decoded outer request-length check before these reads.
operations.response_contract: No response bytes; the helper initializes response length to zero.
completion_codes: 0xd5 wrong platform or reset state already marked 0x15
operations.external_effect: Mutates two in-process reset masks, stores data bytes0..1, marks reset state 0x15, and creates or rearms one or two deferred timers using literal interval 6000. Timer-creation failures are logged without changing the success completion. The timer callbacks and resulting physical reset action are not decoded in this family pass.
operations.activation: Numeric platform-type global must equal 2. Reset state must be exactly idle (zero); state 0x15 and other nonzero states have distinct failures.
operations.channel: No channel predicate or channel-dependent branch is decoded in this operation.
operations.contract_exactness: decoded static control/data flow; opaque cached fields and timer callbacks remain explicitly unnamed

operations.request_contract: No payload byte is consumed by the decoded helper and no handler-level request-length predicate is present.
operations.response_contract: Two cached bytes are returned verbatim; response length is two.
operations.external_effect: Reads two in-process controller/reset bytes. On channel 5 it also clears reset state 0x15 back to zero under a mutex.
operations.channel: Channel 5 is accepted, logs the path, and may clear reset state 0x15; other channels return the same two-byte cache without that mutation.
operations.contract_exactness: decoded static control/data flow; opaque cached fields and timer callbacks remain explicitly unnamed

operations.request_contract: Data byte0 and data byte2 are copied into one of two cached three-byte records. Data byte1 selects record 1 or 2 and must equal 1 or 2. The handler does not consume the outer request-length field before these reads.
operations.response_contract: No response bytes are written by the handler.
operations.external_effect: Replaces the selected cached status record, writes two selector-specific cfgdb attributes, sets the corresponding pending-status bit, and writes a further cfgdb synchronization attribute. Unlike several chassis-family setters, cfgdb failures are surfaced as 0xff.
operations.channel: Channel 5 is accepted and invokes setI2Comn before state/cfgdb mutation; no rejecting channel branch is decoded.
operations.contract_exactness: decoded static control/data flow; opaque cached fields and timer callbacks remain explicitly unnamed

operations.request_contract: Data byte0 selects controller/status record 1 or 2 and must equal 1 or 2. The handler does not consume the outer request-length field before the read.
operations.response_contract: Two bytes: byte0 is constant 0x30; byte1 is status. Status is 2 when the selected pending bit is clear, 3 when pending is set but the selected completion bit is clear, otherwise it is read from selector-specific cfgdb.
operations.external_effect: Reads the two in-process status masks and, only for the completed branch, a selector-specific cfgdb integer. No mutation or channel-specific path is decoded.
operations.channel: No channel predicate or channel-dependent branch is decoded in this operation.
operations.contract_exactness: decoded static control/data flow; opaque cached fields and timer callbacks remain explicitly unnamed

state_machine.stage: 0x30/0x48 accepts target selector 1..3, marks state 0x15, mutates masks, and schedules deferred timers
state_machine.read_stage: 0x30/0x49 returns two cached bytes; a channel-5 read may clear state 0x15
state_machine.sync: 0x30/0x4a accepts record selector 1..2, updates cache and cfgdb, and marks the corresponding pending-status bit
state_machine.query: 0x30/0x4b maps pending/completion masks to status 2 or 3, or returns selector-specific cfgdb status

limits: The semantic names of opaque data bytes and cached globals are not recovered beyond their observed control/data-flow roles.
Timer callbacks were not included in this bounded family pass, so an actual hardware reset is a possible downstream consequence, not a decoded fact here.
No runnable codec or live behavior is claimed.
